_purpose: Machine-readable guardrails. The hooks in .claude/hooks/ read this file at runtime, and .claude/settings.json duplicates the sharpest edges as permission-deny rules for defence in depth. Edit this file via a proposal, same as anything else in operating-layer/ — see operating-layer/OPERATING-RULES.md.
_protected_paths_note: operating-layer/** is deliberately NOT protected here — it is edited via proposals (see propose skill), not locked behind this guard. The line-budget hook (layer_budget.py) is the control on that directory instead.
_blocked_command_patterns_note: Case-insensitive, matched with re.search against the raw command string by guard_commands.py. These are a floor, not a ceiling — they catch the shapes named in OPERATING-RULES.md, not every possible destructive command. A Bash rule is not a security boundary (see the Claude Code permissions docs on wrapper/quoting evasion) — the point is to stop the agent's own straightforward attempt, and to make the stop legible.
_outbound_allowlist_note: Placeholder. Populate with domains/services agents may send outbound messages to (email, chat, webhooks) once you wire an outbound-send hook. Empty means: no enforced allowlist yet, so treat any outbound send as something OPERATING-RULES.md says must go to a person.
